correctness.rationale: The hyperplane distance identity is exact. The scalar strictly convex p-power remainder admits a positive global minimum c_p, integrates pointwise to the full real \(L_p\) space, and yields \(\eta(\varepsilon)\ge c_p\varepsilon^p\) for all radii. Two disjoint normalized indicator coordinates yield a unit-sphere pair with separation at least epsilon and deficit \(c_p\varepsilon^p+O(\varepsilon^{2p})\), hence the full limit. The quartic coefficient follows from an exact rational sum of squares; finite tests were not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The originating 2023 index article and its 2024 follow-up were inspected in full at the relevant results; neither states the claimed \(p>2\) global \(L_p\) coefficient. The 2019 Bregman literature supplies related estimates and possible known scalar constants but not the matching norm-one upper construction. The closest existing local-summand profile has coefficient \(1/p\), which is strictly larger than \(c_p\). Literature uncertainty is explicitly retained.
residual_risks: The cited Xu–Zhang 1989 article was not accessible in full; exact Lp Bregman constants may be known there.

value.rationale: The global index of strong rotundity is a motivated measure of strong exposure introduced in 2023; its exact non-Hilbert small-radius profile has not been calculated in the inspected primary sources. The theorem gives a dimension- and atomicity-independent sharp leading term for every \(p>2\), with a strict quantitative separation from a canonical local profile. The quartic coefficient \(1/12\) provides a simple exact benchmark, while the two-coordinate optimizer gives structural explanation rather than a mere numerical gain.
